about: Every entry is a folder of this repository. A standard's version is the version line of its specification, and each version is tagged as the entry's id, then -v, then the version. The kind is base for the Common Agent Specification, standard for every Common Agent Standard, and guide for a library of playbooks that has no schema to conform to.

standards.name: The Common Agent Specification
standards.summary: The Common Agent Specification defines what an agent is, in terms anyone can check. An agent holds a key that signs, answers five questions for anyone who asks, declares its standing facts in one signed document, refuses what it does not do with a typed answer, and collects signed records of what others have checked about it.

standards.name: Agent Messaging
standards.summary: Agent Messaging describes how agents reach each other over reliable messaging: signed messages that wait in an inbox, events published to every subscriber, and presence. It is a network binding of the agent the Common Agent Specification defines.

standards.name: Personal Agent Naming
standards.summary: Personal Agent Naming names a personal agent on an email address its owner already has. The name is bound to the agent's own key, resolves to the addresses where the agent can be reached, and moves from one registrar to another without changing.

standards.name: Agent Mandate
standards.summary: A mandate is a signed delegation of authority that is bounded and can be revoked. It states which powers are granted, up to what ceiling, within what scope and until when, so the other side can check it before acting.

standards.name: Agent RFP
standards.summary: An Agent RFP is a signed, structured request for proposal. It carries what the buyer wants delivered, what it will hand over, the rights it needs in the result, how acceptance will be measured, what it will pay and the date by which it will decide.

standards.name: Agent SoW
standards.summary: An Agent SoW is a statement of work between two parties whose agents do recurring work together, written so that software can grade its clauses. It records what was agreed, what arrived, what it cost and what happens when the work is contested.

standards.name: Agent Reputations
standards.summary: Agent Reputations holds evidence about how agent interactions went, in a bureau's ledger that cannot be quietly edited afterwards. What one engagement records is what the next one reads first.

standards.name: Agent Roles
standards.summary: Agent Roles is a registry of jobs that recur on every mesh. Each role is a contract with a defined scope, the access it needs and the refusals that define it, and any agent that meets the contract can hold the role.

standards.name: Agent Processes
standards.summary: Agent Processes is a plain-text language for writing down how a piece of work runs: what starts it, the phases it moves through and who holds each one, what crosses each handoff, and how much of each phase an agent may run on its own.

standards.name: Agent Collab
standards.summary: Agent Collab is a library of collaboration playbooks written for agents to fetch, read and follow. Each pattern needs only a shared record that everyone in the cast can read and post to: a room by default, or a message thread or a document's version history. It is a guide with no schema to conform to, and every participant reads the same page before speaking.
